name: Uzzah and the ark
charge: Putting forth his hand to the ark of God, which was carried on a new cart and not on the shoulders of the Levites
summary: David gathered thirty thousand chosen men to bring up the ark of God from the house of Abinadab, where it had been left since the days of the judges, and they set it upon a new cart with Uzzah and Ahio driving and all Israel playing before the Lord. At Nachon’s threshingfloor the oxen shook it, Uzzah put forth his hand and took hold of the ark, and God smote him there for his error, and he died by the ark. Grabbing it was a natural reaction, but the Most High had already declared it holy and untouchable. When David came back for it, none carried it but the Levites, upon their shoulders, after the due order.
offenseFull: The congregation agreed to bring the ark again, because they had not enquired at it in the days of Saul, and the thing was right in the eyes of all the people (1 Chronicles 13:3-4). The purpose was right and the joy was real. They set the ark of God upon a new cart and brought it out of the house of Abinadab, and Uzzah and Ahio the sons of Abinadab drove the cart, with Ahio going before the ark, while David and all the house of Israel played before the Lord on all manner of instruments of fir wood, on harps, psalteries, timbrels, cornets and cymbals (2 Samuel 6:3-5). But the manner of carrying it had already been commanded, and a cart was not it. This is the third of three: touch not, taste not, handle not. The staves were to stay in the rings of the ark and never be taken out of them, so that it was always borne and never handled (Exodus 25:15). The sons of Kohath were the movers of the sanctuary, but when Aaron and his sons had made an end of covering the holy things, the Kohathites came to bear them and were not to touch any holy thing, lest they die (Numbers 4:15). Only the Levites chosen for it could come near. A new cart was what the Philistines used to send the ark home; it was not an improvement on obedience.
judgmentFull: When they came to Nachon’s threshingfloor, the oxen shook the cart and Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God and took hold of it. The anger of the Lord was kindled against him, and God smote him there for his error, and he died there by the ark of God (2 Samuel 6:6-9). It was a natural reaction; the beast bumped the cart and he reached for it. It does not matter. That was the most holy thing and it was not his place to touch it, and even a man who meant well did not get away with it. The Lord had warned Aaron himself, through Moses, not to come at all times into the holy place within the vail before the mercy seat that is upon the ark, so that he die not, and that warning came after the two sons of Aaron died for offering strange fire (Leviticus 16:1-2). Everything in that day had to be done to a T, and we owe thanks that there is mercy through Christ, because the Lord was not playing about His commandments. If it falls, let it fall, and get a Levite to lift it.

David was displeased because the Lord had made a breach upon Uzzah, and he called the place Perez-uzzah; and he was afraid of the Lord that day and asked how the ark of the Lord should come to him. He would not remove it to himself into the city of David, but carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite, where it remained three months, and the Lord blessed Obed-edom and all his household (2 Samuel 6:10-11). David had seen the power of the Lord, and his flesh trembled for fear of Him and he was afraid of His judgments (Psalms 119:120). When he came back for the ark he did not attempt the same journey with more confidence. He said that none ought to carry the ark of God but the Levites, for the Lord had chosen them to carry it and to minister to Him for ever (1 Chronicles 15:2). He charged the chief fathers of the Levites to sanctify themselves, because the Lord their God made a breach upon them at the first, in that they sought Him not after the due order; and the children of the Levites bare the ark upon their shoulders with the staves upon it, as Moses commanded according to the word of the Lord (1 Chronicles 15:12-15). The failure was confessed as the whole nation’s, not laid on one man. The difference between the two
journeys was not whether David wanted to honour the Lord. It was whether the honour was offered in the manner the Lord had appointed.

text.text: And let us bring again the ark of our God to us: for we enquired not at it in the days of Saul.
And all the congregation said that they would do so: for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people.
And they set the ark of God upon a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab that was in Gibeah: and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drave the new cart.
And they brought it out of the house of Abinadab which was at Gibeah, accompanying the ark of God: and Ahio went before the ark.
And David and all the house of Israel played before the Lord on all manner of instruments made of fir wood, even on harps, and on psalteries, and on timbrels, and on cornets, and on cymbals.
The staves shall be in the rings of the ark: they shall not be taken from it.

And when Aaron and his sons have made an end of covering the sanctuary, and all the vessels of the sanctuary, as the camp is to set forward; after that, the sons of Kohath shall come to bear it: but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die. These things are the burden of the sons of Kohath in the tabernacle of the congregation.
And when they came to Nachon’s threshingfloor, Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen shook it.
And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for his error; and there he died by the ark of God.
And David was displeased, because the Lord had made a breach upon Uzzah: and he called the name of the place Perez–uzzah to this day.
And David was afraid of the Lord that day, and said, How shall the ark of the Lord come to me?
And the Lord spake unto Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they offered before the Lord, and died;

And the Lord said unto Moses, Speak unto Aaron thy brother, that he come not at all times into the holy place within the vail before the mercy seat, which is upon the ark; that he die not: for I will appear in the cloud upon the mercy seat.
So David would not remove the ark of the Lord unto him into the city of David: but David carried it aside into the house of Obed–edom the Gittite.
And the ark of the Lord continued in the house of Obed–edom the Gittite three months: and the Lord blessed Obed–edom, and all his household.
My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.
Then David said, None ought to carry the ark of God but the Levites: for them hath the Lord chosen to carry the ark of God, and to minister unto him for ever.

And said unto them, Ye are the chief of the fathers of the Levites: sanctify yourselves, both ye and your brethren, that ye may bring up the ark of the Lord God of Israel unto the place that I have prepared for it.
For because ye did it not at the first, the Lord our God made a breach upon us, for that we sought him not after the due order.
So the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves to bring up the ark of the Lord God of Israel.
And the children of the Levites bare the ark of God upon their shoulders with the staves thereon, as Moses commanded according to the word of the Lord.
